sources.title: Assisted Fibre Inflation in perturbative LVS

evidence.text: Numerically solve covariant second-order background equations using e-fold time and the tree-level Kähler metric, progressing from one to three evolving fields. Extract canonical endpoint distances, slow-roll observables at horizon exit and vacuum mass-matrix eigenvalues.

sources.title: On Global Embeddings of Assisted Fibre Inflation

evidence.text: Combine BBHL α′³ and logarithmic loop corrections to stabilize the volume perturbatively. Add winding-loop and higher-derivative F4 contributions to lift the remaining Kähler directions, together with a modeled uplift term.

sources.title: Tetra-quadric CY Threefold and Assisted Fibre Inflation

evidence.text: Effective excursion is computed as trajectory length ∫sqrt(Gab Φ′aΦ′b)dN=∫sqrt(2εH)dN. Individual comparison distances are obtained by varying one modulus with the other two fixed at their minima.

sources.title: Assisted Fibre Inflation in perturbative LVS

evidence.text: Build the scalar potential from BBHL α′³ and logarithmic loop terms stabilizing the volume, winding-loop and higher-derivative F4 terms lifting fiber directions, plus Cup/V^p uplift. The geometric setup has no conventional KK-loop contribution in the stated construction.

sources.title: On Global Embeddings of Assisted Fibre Inflation

evidence.text: Numerically integrate covariant multi-field background equations using e-fold time, the tree-level Kähler metric and the corrected scalar potential. Report trajectories, slow-roll observables, mass eigenvalues and evolving KK/string scales.

sources.title: Tetra-quadric CY Threefold and Assisted Fibre Inflation

evidence.text: The potential combines BBHL α′³ and logarithmic loop terms, a phenomenological uplift Cup/V^p, winding-loop corrections, and higher-derivative F4 terms. Analytic stepwise stabilization is explanatory; numerical minima are obtained by treating all four volume fields simultaneously.

sources.title: The Octagon at large M

evidence.text: The Octagon quiver provides the ultraviolet string construction whose cascade must end in a viable supersymmetry-breaking theory. Fractional-brane and orientifold rank shifts overlap on some faces but differ on face 2, a distinction used in the proposed bulk interpretation.

sources.title: String Theory Realizations of the Nilpotent Goldstino

evidence.text: Open-string Chan–Paton orientifold projections determine the spectrum. Annulus/Möbius open–closed duality explains the extra Ramond-sector sign through the antibrane's reversed RR charge.

sources.title: Supersymmetry Breaking Warped Throats and the Weak Gravity Conjecture

evidence.text: Compare tension-mediated NSNS and charge-mediated RR exchange in common units. Force signs diagnose long-distance motion; separate tachyon or duality information supplies short-distance and nonperturbative channels.

sources.title: String Phenomenology From a Worldsheet Perspective

evidence.text: Fix the basis, enumerate allowed phase assignments, construct sectors and apply their projections. Classify the resulting spectra by gauge group, chirality and unwanted states. In this paper, the operation is proposed for searches extending beyond the displayed six- and three-generation examples.

sources.title: The Octagon at large M

evidence.text: A proposed dimer partial resolution is tested by checking whether the adjacent gauge factors can have equal ranks. Fractional-brane and orientifold rank shifts obstruct the face fusion used to realize the dangerous resolutions.

sources.title: Heterotic strings on Enriques surfaces

evidence.text: Classify E8×E8 shifts using Kac’s algorithm and extended Dynkin diagrams. For Spin(32)/Z2, separate integral and half-integral 4w classes. Equivalence uses gauge-lattice translations and Weyl transformations stabilizing the fixed v.

sources.title: Brane supersymmetry breaking

evidence.text: Construct torus, Klein-bottle, annulus, and Möbius amplitudes using SO(4) characters. Impose closed-sector modular invariance, crosscap consistency, open-spectrum positivity, and RR tadpole cancellation; use S and P transformations between channels.

sources.title: String Phenomenology From a Worldsheet Perspective

evidence.text: Can a worldsheet construction produce phenomenologically useful non-supersymmetric vacua, and how can their low-energy EFT descriptions be recovered? The paper explores tachyon projection and relations between worldsheet supersymmetry classes as two approaches.

sources.title: Stability and vacuum energy in open string models with broken supersymmetry

evidence.text: How do orientifold-compatible brane positions determine the massless spectrum and one-loop vacuum energy after supersymmetry is broken along a circle? The T-dual description makes Wilson lines geometric and separates endpoint half-branes from mirror-paired stacks.

sources.title: The cosmological constant and dark dimensions from non-supersymmetric strings

evidence.text: Can non-supersymmetric strings cancel gauge/matter one-loop vacuum energy despite string-scale brane supersymmetry breaking, while bulk contributions track large extra dimensions and moduli dynamics generate a dark-energy scale?

sources.title: Dark Horse, Dark Matter: Revisiting the $SO$(16)x $SO$(16)' Nonsupersymmetric Model in the LHC and Dark Energy Era

evidence.text: Can a nonsupersymmetric, tachyon-free heterotic model supply an effective framework for visible matter, dark sectors and cosmology? The paper studies this question using a reviewed ten-dimensional SO(16) × SO(16)' construction and mostly low-energy descriptions.

sources.title: String Defects, Supersymmetry and the Swampland

evidence.text: Which string-defect consistency conditions constrain six-dimensional supergravity beyond anomaly cancellation, and how do explicit orientifolds delimit their applicability to BPS defects, stable non-BPS defects and localized supersymmetry breaking?

evidence.text: How do freely acting, especially asymmetric, type II orbifolds realize spontaneous supersymmetry breaking, constrained moduli spaces and consistent brane spectra, and what do their infinite-distance limits imply for swampland conjectures?

sources.title: Open strings

destinations.title: Do string loop corrections from D-branes and O-planes invalidate large-volume stabilization or its soft supersymmetry-breaking predictions, particularly the suppressed gaugino masses?

Under what spectrum and charge conditions does the exponentially suppressed one-loop cosmological constant of nonsupersymmetric Scherk–Schwarz heterotic models remain suppressed at two loops, and what might extend to higher orders?

These three constructions provide explicit string settings without supersymmetric protection of vacuum energy. Their gravitational tadpoles produce positive dilaton runaways that compete with flux and internal curvature.

Can an accidentally suppressed one-loop string vacuum energy balance a generic two-loop contribution to stabilize the dilaton and geometric moduli at weak coupling, with numerical separation between the AdS and compactification scales?
Can a string vacuum with supersymmetry broken at the string scale have vanishing perturbative cosmological constant, and can the cancellation extend beyond the first two loops?

Does the two-loop cosmological constant still vanish in two special nonsupersymmetric type II models once coincident picture-changing-operator singularities and potentially finite collision terms are included?
